newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Labour won the General Election with a historic landslide and the greatest swing of votes since 1945. Six Cabinet ministers were among the hordes of Conservative MPs to lose their seats. At present Labour's majority is projected to reach a massive 174 seats.
- SIZE OF LABOUR'S WIN CONFUSES THE MARKETS

The size of Labour's election victory caused a degree of confusion in the markets, causing the pound to move higher while gilts fell slightly. Dealers are fearing a possible 1 to 2 percent fall in share prices.
- GAIN AND PAIN IN THE GREAT 10M STG GAMBLE

Around 10m stg was gambled on this election at fixed-odds bookmakers alone, the largest gambling election ever. While Labour have been the hot favourites throughout the campaign, Ladbrokes said that money placed on the Tories to do well in defeat covered a great deal of their liability.

BZW staff in New York watched the General Election on television on the 106th floor of the World Trade Center. The bank's chief US economist Chris Iggo said the Labour landslide was likely to deter the new government from doing anything extreme as they will be aiming for two terms in government.
